1. **Ensure NVIDIA Drivers and CUDA are Installed**: Make sure that you have the latest NVIDIA drivers and CUDA toolkit installed on your system. This is crucial for any application to utilize GPU resources.

2. **Install NVIDIA Docker (nvidia-docker2)**: NVIDIA provides a tool called `nvidia-docker2` that allows Docker containers to leverage GPU resources. You can install it with the following commands (on a system using APT package manager):

   ```bash
   distribution=$(. /etc/os-release;echo $ID$VERSION_ID)
   curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | sudo apt-key add -
   curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-docker2
   sudo systemctl restart docker
   ```

3. **Configure Docker to Use NVIDIA Runtime**: By default, Docker containers do not have access to the GPU. You need to specify the NVIDIA runtime when starting the container. This can typically be done with the `--gpus` flag.

4. **Start the Ollama Container**: Assuming you have a Docker image for Ollama, you can start it with GPU access by using a command similar to this:

   ```bash
   docker run --gpus all -it <ollama-image-name>
   ```

   The `--gpus all` flag tells Docker to make all available GPUs accessible to the container. Replace `<ollama-image-name>` with the actual name of the Ollama Docker image you are using.

5. **Verify GPU Access**: Once the container is running, you can verify that it has access to the GPUs by running a GPU-aware command or application inside the container that can report GPU usage or availability.

Please note that the specifics can vary depending on your system configuration, the version of Docker, and the Ollama project's requirements. For the most accurate and detailed instructions, it would be best to consult the official Ollama documentation or the community forums related to the project.
